retained_initial_conclusions: Request a: N=3; actual-send TTFT=30 ms; planned-origin TTFT=50 ms; exact TPOT=10 ms; normal protocol latency=60 ms. (60-30)/(3-1)=15 ms is not exact TPOT because the FINAL tail is averaged into token intervals.

Request b: N=2 with only a single 2-token chunk; actual-send TTFT=30 ms, planned-origin TTFT=30 ms, normal protocol latency=120 ms. Exact TPOT and exact ITL are not recoverable from chunk-only evidence; (120-30)/(2-1)=90 ms is not TPOT.

Request c: N=0 and no normal FINAL; TIMEOUT at 140 is a logical termination, not normal completion. TTFT, TPOT, and the protocol-minus-TTFT projection are undefined; termination latency 45 ms is retained.

Output-token throughput: [0,100) emission window=5 tokens/100 ms=50 tokens/s (a=3, b=2, c=0, including b not certified good); normal-completion window=3 tokens from a/100 ms=30 tokens/s; arrival cohort through H=150 has 5 output tokens/150 ms=33.3333333333 tokens/s. These are different populations and windows and are not goodput.
Admissions: by H there are 3 actual service admission decisions but 2 effective business admissions (a and b); c's late actual acceptance at 145 does not revive its TIMEOUT at 140.

Goodput at J=150 and J=180: a is certified good, b remains unknown, c failed; counts offered=3, certified good=1, possible unknown=1, definite failure=1; certified-goodput=6.6666666667 requests/s, identification upper bound=13.3333333333 requests/s, qualified fraction bounds [0.3333333333,0.6666666667]. These are deterministic identification bounds on three requests, not confidence intervals. b's quality PASS by J=180 does not recover exact TPOT from one 2-token chunk.

Two-by-two descriptive effects: low load -3 ms, high load +2 ms, interaction +5 ms; the change is not uniformly faster. This is one descriptive table without repetitions, uncertainty, or carryover control.

A pooled p99 over the observed 200 requests can be descriptive only if the percentile definition, population, and window are stated. It is not 200 independent service repetitions: requests are correlated within runs, the two runs provide at most two run-level units, and all-baseline-before-all-changed ordering confounds condition with time, drift, warmup, cache, and environment.

Under the separate stipulated iid fixed-sample Bernoulli model, zero violations in n=200 at one-sided alpha=0.05 gives q_U = 1 - 0.05^(1/200) = 0.014867039 (1.4867039%), so it does not support a below-1% claim. A strict below-1% zero-violation single final look requires at least 299 independent iid trials; the two correlated service runs do not inherit this model.

Final initial decision retained: reject claims of uniform speedup, independent pooled-p99 evidence, and establishment of a below-1% violation rate from zero violations in 200 trials; accept only directly computed request-a success and window-specific output-token rates; b unknown, c failed, and c's late acceptance is not effective admission.

Initial experimental proposal retained as a plan, not an executed result: independent unit is a complete run/block, not a request; balanced/randomized baseline/changed order; separate profiling; run-level or hierarchical analysis; fresh confirmation units; no opportunistic extension or adding looks after seeing results.

request_x_timing.calculation: TTFT = first client token 25 - send 0 = 25 ms. With explicit token times 25, 34, 47, exact TPOT = (47-25)/(3-1) = 11 ms; ITLs are 9 and 13 ms. Quality latency is not used in either timing calculation.
request_x_timing.note: Producer-complete immutable output v17 exists at 18 ms, and cert-1 at 22 ms binds to v17/rule-7 before the first client token at 25 ms and before FINAL at 60 ms. Quality is evidence about a complete production-side output, not a client-visible completion event, so early certification is legitimate. The certificate does not define TTFT or TPOT. No joint SLO threshold is restated for this fixture, so quality evidence alone does not establish full joint goodput.

evidence_at_J_80.duplicate_evidence: cert-1 at 22 ms for v17/rule-7 PASS appears twice with the same certificate identity, time, output version, rule, and verdict. This is an exact duplicate export and is idempotently reduced to one PASS; it is not a contradiction.
evidence_at_J_80.request_x_quality_status: Within the J=80 evidence view, x has one deduplicated PASS for v17/rule-7. x also has normal FINAL at 60 ms <= H=80, so its service completion is in the H snapshot. Whether x is a certified good completion additionally requires the fixed joint SLO and output/stop conditions; if the earlier illustrative TTFT<=35 ms, exact TPOT<=15 ms, nonempty-output contract were explicitly reused, x's 25/11 timing would also satisfy it, but that threshold is not restated here.
evidence_at_J_80.request_y_status: At H=80, y is admitted and still in business progress: token times 72 and 76 are visible, but protocol FINAL is 98 ms > H, so y has no normal completion by H. Its client timing is observable as TTFT=72-10=62 ms, exact TPOT=(76-72)/(2-1)=4 ms, and protocol latency=98-10=88 ms, but the fixed H=80 snapshot does not count y as completed or as a potential-good completed request. Its cert at 70 ms binds to v8/rule-7 but is diagnostic only for the H=80 snapshot; it cannot create or enlarge a completion.

evidence_at_J_100.request_x_conflict: cert-2 at 90 ms is FAIL for the same output version v17 and the same fixed rule-7. The earlier PASS and later FAIL are deterministic contradictory certificates for one fixed output and rule identity, not a legitimate rule revision and not an identity-payload duplicate. The status is CONFLICT; qualification settlement is UNRESOLVED. The implementation must not silently choose the latest FAIL, nor silently keep the earlier PASS.
evidence_at_J_100.duplicate_at_J_100: The duplicate cert-1 remains one idempotent PASS; it does not cancel or override the later contradictory FAIL.
evidence_at_J_100.request_y_at_J_100: The PASS for v8/rule-7 is available by J=100, but y's FINAL at 98 ms is still after H=80. J=100 is an evidence cutoff, not a new service cutoff: it does not make y complete in the original H=80 snapshot. To count y as completed, a separate report must use a new service observation with H' >= 98 ms; within that new H' snapshot the existing v8/rule-7 PASS can bind to the same v8 output, subject to the fixed joint SLO and output conditions.
evidence_at_J_100.later_evidence_rule: Later quality evidence can fill or revise a quality label for an output already normal-completed by H, but it cannot move H, add a post-H completion, or rewrite service-event times. A later J changes the evidence view only.

new_quality_fixture_reasoning.preserve_earlier_report: Keep the H=80 service snapshot and the J=80 evidence report immutable and auditable: x has FINAL at 60 ms and one deduplicated PASS; y is still in progress at H. Publish J=100 as a new evidence revision that reuses the same H=80 service snapshot, records cert-1 once, records cert-2, marks x's quality as CONFLICT and its qualification as UNRESOLVED, and leaves y unfinished in the original snapshot. Do not overwrite the earlier J=80 report as though the conflict had always been present; keep both reports with their H, J, certificate identities, output versions, rule identity, duplicate-dedup record, conflict record, and unresolved status. Do not convert a conflict into a new rule or use a later PASS/FAIL as a silent correction.
new_quality_fixture_reasoning.physical_completion: A quality certificate, producer-complete immutable output, and logical FINAL are separate from physical resource completion. Quality evidence says something about an identified output and rule, not that the client consumed it, protocol buffers flushed, device work finished, KV/workspace was released, network buffers drained, or in-flight accesses ended. Likewise, a logical timeout or other business terminal state closes business eligibility but does not prove physical resource completion. Capacity release requires no business retention and completion of all in-flight accesses; producer completion or quality certification alone does not establish that.

revised_experiment_plan.scope: This remains a proposed design only. No device experiment, service measurement, independent confirmation, real quality evaluation, or general Agent benefit is claimed.

two_run_p99_redesign.unit: The independent unit is a complete service/process run or a predeclared randomized time block. Requests and tokens within a run are correlated and are not independent repetitions; two runs provide at most two run-level units.
two_run_p99_redesign.assignment: Predefine multiple blocks and randomize or balance baseline and changed order within each block, for example ABBA or a randomized complete block ordering. Do not run all baseline before all changed.
two_run_p99_redesign.repetitions: Use a pilot to characterize run-level variance and tail-event frequency, then predefine the number of independent runs and requests per run. Do not treat pooled requests as independent repetitions and do not extend opportunistically after seeing results.
two_run_p99_redesign.warmup: For steady-state comparisons, require declared path coverage and no pending preparation before opening the measurement window. Keep FULL_COLD, LOADED_COLD, and diagnostic profiling runs separate from primary steady-state timing.
two_run_p99_redesign.timing: Primary performance runs use minimal instrumentation and the same workload, arrival process, cache state, H, J, joint SLO, output/stop rules, and quality rules. Detailed profiling runs are separate diagnostics and are not pooled with normal runs.
two_run_p99_redesign.quality_and_snapshot: Freeze the H service snapshot and J evidence view separately. Count normal completions by H only; bind certificates to the immutable output version and fixed rule; deduplicate identical certificate identities/payloads; preserve any same-output/fixed-rule PASS/FAIL or identity-load conflict as CONFLICT and report qualification as UNRESOLVED. UNKNOWN is not PASS. Later J may update evidence for an H-completed output but cannot move H or add post-H completions; a new H requires a new service observation version.
two_run_p99_redesign.analysis: Analyze at the run/block level or with a pre-specified hierarchical model. Report pooled p99 only descriptively unless the model supports an interval. Retain failures, timeouts, unknowns, conflicts, and the complete offered-request accounting.

independent_confirmation_design.freeze: Freeze the candidate, joint SLO, task and quality oracle, output/rule identity, H and J, workload, analysis method, resource budget, and decision rules before confirmation. Use fresh independent units that did not participate in exploration, profiling, selection, or prior confirmation.
independent_confirmation_design.iid_bernoulli_branch: Only under the separate stipulated iid fixed-sample Bernoulli model: for a single final look, preselect n=299 independent units and require zero violations for a strict 95% one-sided upper bound below 1%. With n=200, zero violations gives about 1.4867% and does not support a below-1% claim. These must be genuinely independent trials under that model, not 299 correlated requests.
independent_confirmation_design.planned_looks: If planned looks are used, preselect all cumulative n_j and alpha_j with sum alpha_j <= 0.05, use exact one-sided tests at each look, and stop only at the planned looks. Do not add looks, change endpoints, or treat an exploration result as fresh confirmation.
independent_confirmation_design.correlated_service_runs: For correlated service runs, the independent unit must be the run/block, not the request. Two correlated runs provide at most two independent units and cannot support a 1% tail claim. If the independent-unit model is not defensible, the conclusion remains unresolved.
independent_confirmation_design.decision_rule: Confirm a below-1% violation rate only if the final valid one-sided upper bound is below 0.01 under the stipulated model. If any violation occurs, do not use the zero-violation formula; use the appropriate full binomial or hierarchical procedure, or report not confirmed. Hard quality failure rejects confirmation; conflicts and unknowns are not counted as good.
independent_confirmation_design.reporting: Report raw event counts, offered/admitted/completed/failed states, H and J, duplicate dedup, conflicts, unknown and failure reasons, window definitions, and model scope. Do not substitute output-token throughput for goodput, do not treat a pooled p99 as independent evidence, and do not claim measured service performance or general Agent benefit from this plan.

limits: No implementation source, author checks, tools, review reports, device experiments, service measurements, or independent measurements are provided; all conclusions use only the supplied scenario and contracts. The experimental plan is not an executed result.

Request b's exact TPOT and ITL cannot be recovered from a single 2-token chunk; b remains unknown even at J=180. The initial goodput ranges are deterministic identification bounds on three requests, not confidence intervals.

The initial throughput rates use different populations and windows; they must not be substituted for goodput. The two-by-two table is one descriptive table without repetitions, uncertainty, or carryover control.

The pooled 200-request p99 is pseudo-replicated across correlated requests, provides at most two run-level units, and is confounded by all-baseline-before-all-changed ordering; it is descriptive only.
The Bernoulli zero-violation bound is valid only under the separate stipulated iid fixed-sample model; it does not apply to the two correlated service runs.

No joint SLO threshold is restated for x and y. Their TTFT/TPOT values and quality certificates alone do not establish full goodput; any reuse of the earlier illustrative TTFT<=35 ms, exact TPOT<=15 ms thresholds must be stated explicitly.

At J=80 x has one idempotent quality PASS and normal FINAL by H; at J=100 the same v17/rule-7 output has contradictory PASS and FAIL certificates, so quality is CONFLICT and qualification is UNRESOLVED. The conflict cannot be resolved by latest-writer selection or by treating it as a rule revision.

y's FINAL at 98 ms is after H=80, so y is not a completed request in the original H=80 snapshot even at J=100. J cannot enlarge H; including y requires a new service observation with H' >= 98 ms, using the existing v8/rule-7 PASS only if the output and joint conditions otherwise qualify.

Quality evidence, producer-complete immutable output, protocol FINAL, and logical timeout are not proof of physical resource completion. Capacity release requires no business retention and completion of all in-flight accesses.

No measured service performance, real quality evaluator, tokenizer, network, GPU, load generator, clock calibration, or general Agent benefit is claimed; all confirmation and p99 designs require actual independent data and validity checks before use.
